Q17 The Delete button is now shown only while no task belongs to the project. The senior's reason: the server already refuses to delete a project with tasks, and every project in use has some, so the button could only fail. Keep it hidden that way, or always show it and let the refusal explain? Recommend: keep hidden; a button that can only fail is noise.

Q18 Ended tasks are grouped last, below Finished, rather than hidden behind a toggle. Fine by me; say if you'd rather they be collapsed.

Q19 Dismissed tasks were left undecided; today the overview keeps showing them in their group with their actions greyed out. Leave it in open-items, or decide now (for instance: a dismissed task leaves the overview)? Recommend: leave it; nothing forces it yet.

- Delete: `internal/server/gui_projects.go` `postDeleteProject`; the page asks `projectInUse` (`internal/server/projects.go:25`) whether to show it.
- Tests: `internal/server/gui_projects_internal_test.go`, grouping with dismissed tasks kept, and `projectInUse`.
- Recorded in open-items by the senior: dismissed tasks on the overview; the Tasks page and the overview sort differently.

Open: Q17 Delete hidden while tasks exist; Q18 ended tasks grouped last; Q19 dismissed tasks on the overview. Next: your look at the page, then I close out whatever you flip.

content.text:
Q17 is bigger than a button: the server never deletes a task today, so "cascade" means inventing task-record deletion. Q18 and Q19 are settled as you said. One question decides how the cascade works, then I dispatch it as a follow-up change.

Q20 What deleting a project with tasks does. Background: ten tables reference a task (events, logs, comments, artifacts, requests, and so on), and nothing deletes those rows today; the only destructive act on a task is dismissal, which makes the runner delete its record, spool and workspace while the server keeps the task row and its log.

a. cascade, allowed only once every task in the project is dismissed: the project delete then removes those tasks' server records (rows, events, logs, comments, artifacts). The Delete button appears when the project has no undismissed task. Dismissal stays the one act that ends a task on a runner;
b. cascade in one click: deleting the project stops and dismisses every live task in it, then removes the records. Destroys work in flight;
c. detach: the project goes, its tasks lose their project and stay on the Tasks page. No task deletion anywhere.

Recommend: (a); it reuses dismissal as the destructive step so nothing live is destroyed by a project delete, and the logs you would lose are those of tasks you already dismissed.

The change needs a record of its own (it changes "409 while a task belongs" and introduces task-record deletion); I'll have the senior write it short, then the code, in one dispatch, unless you want to read the record first.

## Context and evidence

- Refusal today: `internal/server/projects.go:37-49` (`deleteProject` counts tasks, returns `errProjectInUse`); documented at `docs/operating.md:33`. No accepted ADR decides it (grep across `docs/adr/` finds project deletion nowhere).
- Tables referencing tasks: `internal/server/schema.sql:28,36` and `internal/server/store.go:16-53` (retry_of, comments, artifacts, requests, task_links, stop_notes, placements, notifications).
- Dismissal semantics: `docs/adr/0011-dismissing-finished-tasks.md:12-16, 23-26` ("the runner deletes the task's record, spool and workspace, and the task takes no more follow-ups").
- Q18 and Q19 stand as built.

Open: Q20 (a), (b) or (c). Next: dispatch the project-delete change with the record; then the session's work is the three overview commits on the tip, unpushed, for you to push when ready.
